deferred_source_units.reason: This unit contains the song-and-psalm attribution to Asaph. The general heading alone did not establish a particular literary relationship or an identifiable occasion; no historical Asaph identity was inferred.

The native coalition-list unit names Idumeans, Ishmaelites, Moab and Hagarenes. Its precise coalition and occasion are not established by the differently composed force in the read Chronicles account; the proposed historical identification remains a separate unretained candidate.

This continuation names Gebal, Ammon, Amalek, foreigners and Tyre inhabitants. No sufficiently particular account identifying this combination and its counsel was established; shared people names or generic warfare alone would not identify the episode.

The actual continuation has the valley of weeping, movement toward an appointed place and blessings given by the lawgiver. No sufficiently particular counterpart to this combination was established; familiar springs or rainfall were not supplied to replace the wording.

The unit asks the Lord God of powers and God of Jacob to hear prayer. A particular relationship beyond these common divine addresses and an ordinary request for hearing was not established in this pass.

The source is the general heading for the end and for the sons of Korah. Its broad attribution and designation alone do not establish a particular occasion or a sufficiently distinctive heading comparison.

The heading names a prayer for David and the petition asks hearing because the speaker is poor and needy. No particular Davidic episode or sufficiently specific counterpart beyond the widespread hearing-and-need formula was established.

This unit requests mercy and promises crying to God all day. A sufficiently particular correspondence beyond that common petition and duration was not established; an unexpressed occasion was not assigned.

The source asks God to give ear to the prayer and attend to the voice of petition. No sufficiently particular relationship beyond the ordinary vocabulary of requesting divine hearing was established in this pass.

Raab, Babylon, foreigners, Tyre and Ethiopians appear with a statement that these were born there. The antecedent and identities needed for a particular historical or birth-register comparison remain uncertain; Raab was not silently renamed Egypt and the birthplace was not supplied.

The petition asks that prayer enter before God and that He incline His ear. No particular correspondence beyond common language for a prayer being received was established, and the speaker or occasion was not identified from the heading.

The speaker describes poverty and toils from youth and says that after being raised up he was humbled and left helpless. No particular counterpart to that actual sequence was established; a royal biography or a different order of exaltation and humiliation was not supplied.

The heading identifies understanding and Ethan the Israelite without ancestry or an occasion. The independently read Ethan and Gaithan entries do not resolve which person is intended; those proposed identities are separately preserved at zero credit.

The unit combines an address to the Lord God of powers, a question of incomparability, divine might and surrounding truth. No additional particular relationship beyond these broad praise expressions was established; surrounding truth was not changed into a different attribute.

The enemies reproach the exchange of the anointed. The meaning of exchange and the precise object of the reproach remain unresolved; the read mockery of Jesus does not establish the proposed identification or justify replacing exchange with footsteps.

unresolved_candidates.relationship: Unresolved identification of the hostile coalition
unresolved_candidates.rationale: The source list begins with Idumeans, Ishmaelites, Moab and Hagarenes and continues with further peoples. Chronicles describes a differently composed force against Jehoshaphat. Shared regional enemies do not establish that these are the same coalition or that the psalm describes this battle; the full ensuing battle context was read.

unresolved_candidates.relationship: Unresolved identity of Heman the Israelite
unresolved_candidates.rationale: The heading names Heman the Israelite without a patronymic. Chronicles names Heman the psalm singer with Joel and Samuel in his ancestry, and its surrounding genealogy places him among the Kaathites. Musical association and the shared name do not by themselves establish this precise identification; the additional Heman entry in 1 Chronicles 2:6 was also read.

unresolved_candidates.relationship: Unresolved identity of Ethan the Israelite
unresolved_candidates.rationale: The heading supplies Ethan the Israelite but no ancestry. Chronicles places its Ethan, son of Kisai, in the Merarite singers genealogy. The shared name does not resolve the heading against the Ethan listed among Zara's sons in 1 Chronicles 2:6-8; neither identity is credited.

The actual Kings unit names Gaithan the Ezraite among people surpassed by Solomon in wisdom, whereas the psalm names Ethan the Israelite. The name and designation differ, and the contexts do not establish an identity. Familiar wording from another edition was not substituted.

unresolved_candidates.relationship: Unresolved identification of the proud defeated figure
unresolved_candidates.rationale: The psalm humbles an unnamed proud one like a wounded man. The actual Isaiah address is to Jerusalem, speaks of her arm and then of making the sea desolate and its depths a crossing road; it does not name Rahab or describe the anticipated wounded proud figure. Those familiar details cannot resolve an identity from the supplied texts.

unresolved_candidates.relationship: Unresolved identification of the reproached exchange
unresolved_candidates.rationale: The psalm speaks of enemies reproaching the exchange of the anointed, an expression not resolved by its context. Matthew records abuse of Jesus and mockery that calls Him King of Israel, but does not explain that exchange. An identification of the psalmic event with this Passion scene is therefore unretained.

The proposed comparison anticipated dung language in Jeremiah 8:2. The complete actual text instead calls the unburied bones an example upon the earth's surface. That anticipated verbal correspondence is absent, and the En-dor victims are not identified with these bones. The distinct supported dung-image target is Jeremiah 32:33.

The source calls the Holy One of Israel our King. The actual Isaiah clause says the Lord God, the Holy One, presented Israel as your king; it does not supply the anticipated same divine-kingship predication. The original proposal is unretained rather than normalized; the separately read Isaiah 44:6 expressly calls God Israel's King.

precision_notes: All source words, original complete units, continuation paragraphs and supplied numbering are preserved; familiar Hebrew or English Psalm wording and numbering were not imported.

Limited literary and image comparisons do not assert identical historical events. The coalition identification, Heman and Ethan identities, and the reproached exchange remain separate unretained candidates or source deferrals.

The source retains the turtledove, the lawgiver, God appearing in Zion, being cast aside, inward speech, the heart rejoicing to fear, Mother Zion, physicians, and acquaintances removed because of misery.
Psalm 88 retains plural chosen ones, north and seas, the unnamed proud one, consecrated thing, fortifications made cowardice, removal from purification and the exchange of the anointed.
David, his offspring and Israel remain distinct recipients in the royal promises. Samuel as a historical actor is distinguished from the books named 1 Samuel and 2 Samuel.

Two attempted wording correspondences were not present in the actual targets: Jeremiah 8:2 has an example rather than dung; Isaiah 43:15 presents Israel as king. Their separate precise supported targets are Jeremiah 32:33 and Isaiah 44:6.
Two unavailable Revelation locator hints remain unread and zero credit, separately archived and excluded from the eight actual read candidates and from all target-unit counts.
